note: Documented public statements and votes on Flock / ALPRs. Not a Case_ID catalog. Incomplete on purpose. Hedge rows are not bans.

records.Name: Bernie Sanders
records.What: Posted “STOP AI MASS SURVEILLANCE. STOP FLOCK.” No Senate ban bill in Aug. 20 Washington Times reporting.

records.Name: Tim Burchett
records.What: Introduced H.R. 9800 to cut federal money for Flock-style ALPRs, biometrics, and mass-surveillance imaging.

records.Name: Thomas Massie
records.What: Said he would sponsor a bill to withhold federal money from cities and departments that deploy Flock-style cameras. Formal text was not out in that coverage.

records.Name: Josh Hawley
records.Office: U.S. Senate (R-Mo.); Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism chair
records.What: Opened a Senate Judiciary subcommittee investigation into Flock data collection, retention, and sales. CEO Garrett Langley must produce documents by Sept. 8, 2026.

records.Name: Ron DeSantis
records.What: Said ALPRs including Flock are “out of control,” warned of a surveillance state, and quoted ordinary travel: “It's really none of the government's damn business.” Urged legislative guardrails; FDOT then revoked state-highway ALPR permits for 30-day removal.

records.Name: Greg Abbott
records.What: Ordered Texas state agencies to pause funding for Flock cameras. Local contracts and existing cameras stay unless cities or counties end them; spokesman said most city Flock money is federal.

records.Name: Lois Kolkhorst
records.What: Called for an ALPR ban in a “Get the Flock Out of Texas!” post and said the Senate will take up the issue when the 90th Legislature convenes in January.

records.Name: Josh Shapiro
records.What: Said he would welcome bipartisan legislation banning Flock cameras statewide and that State Police do not use them. Called the cameras not in the public interest.

records.Name: Al Cutrona
records.What: Will introduce a bill barring sale or sharing of plate-reader data with third parties, requiring deletion after 10 days, and making personal misuse a fourth-degree felony.

records.Name: Levi Dean
records.What: Drafting a separate Ohio measure requiring warrants for government ALPR searches and banning AI-assisted government surveillance cameras, with limits on government use of private camera data.

records.Name: Arthur Orr
records.What: Plans post–Nov. 3 legislation for statewide ALPR guardrails—including possible ban. Said the status quo on ~2,800 Flock cameras is “totally unacceptable.”

records.Name: Robert Stewart
records.What: Said he wants to see change on Alabama Flock / ALPR rules before the 2027 legislative session.

records.Name: Michaela Barnett
records.Office: Democratic nominee, U.S. House Tennessee 2nd District
records.What: Agrees with Burchett that license-plate readers are mass surveillance.

records.Name: Jack Johnson
records.What: Drew a line between targeted plate searches and 24-hour surveillance of all citizens. Said liberty wins when it is in question.

records.Name: Jerri Green
records.Office: Democratic nominee for governor; Memphis City Council
records.What: Called for strict guardrails on retention and sharing, including a bar on sharing local surveillance with federal immigration authorities.

records.Name: Page Walley
records.What: Sponsored the PEEPS Act (SB 2215) to require warrants and logging for historical location data, including LPR reads. The bill stalled in subcommittee.

records.Name: Bud Hulsey
records.What: House sponsor of the PEEPS Act companion (HB 2608). The bill stalled in subcommittee.

records.Name: Timothy Hill
records.What: House sponsor of the PEEPS Act companion (HB 2608). The bill stalled in subcommittee.

records.Name: Terry Frank
records.What: Set a Sept. 10 public hearing on LPRs; wants a regulatory framework; raised warrantless mass-surveillance concerns. SO runs 4 cameras.

records.Name: Glenn Jacobs
records.What: Said ALPRs have no place in Knox County and told Fox News Flock needs a nationwide pause until constitutional guardrails catch up.

records.Name: Knox County Commission
records.What: Unanimously passed an emergency ordinance banning fixed ALPRs and ordering removal of about 143 Flock cameras within 30 days.

records.Name: Jeffrey Cassidy
records.What: Suspended 10 Flock cameras. Commission then voted 18–0 not to renew. Contract ends January 2027.

records.Name: Derrick Hutchings
records.What: Commission rescinded Flock authorization after stripping camera funding in June.

records.Name: Denny Wayne Robinson
records.What: Voted no on keeping camera money in June. Commission later rescinded Flock authorization.

records.Name: Adam Thompson
records.What: Said he was blindsided by a ~300-camera plan and introduced a review resolution for privacy, access, audit, and sharing policies before further expansion.

records.Name: Jason Zachary
records.What: Flagged Flock’s open data-access model versus closed systems. That is a vendor-architecture argument, not an exit from plate readers.

records.Name: Dave Rosenberg
records.What: Sponsored a 2017 ordinance banning right-of-way plate scanners and voted no on the 2023 LPR expansion.

records.Name: Nashville Metro Council no votes (14)
records.What: Fourteen members voted against full LPR implementation after the pilot.

records.Name: Freddie O’Connell
records.Office: Mayor of Nashville; former Metro Councilmember
records.What: Voted no on 2023 expansion as a councilmember and has kept dedicated LPR funding out of recent budgets, while still saying LPRs can have investigative value.

records.Name: Sharon Hurt
records.What: Voted no on full LPR implementation, warning biased users can turn “neutral” tools against people.

records.Name: Sandra Sepulveda
records.What: Opposed expansion over lack of written protections and oversight.

records.Name: Colby Sledge
records.What: Co-sponsored the 2017 surveillance-oversight ordinance and voted no on the 2023 LPR expansion.

records.Name: Amelia Parker
records.What: Voted against Knoxville’s Axon / RTIC surveillance package. Argued policy must precede contracts.

records.Name: Seema Singh
records.What: Voted against Knoxville’s Axon / RTIC surveillance package.

records.Name: Rollin Horton
records.What: Opposed a state bill that would have preempted Metro’s local LPR and surveillance rules.

records.Name: Clarksville City Council no votes (6)
records.What: Six members voted against an LPR support resolution: Redd, Marquis, Smith, Allen, Reynolds, and Butler.

records.Name: Karen Reynolds
records.What: Cited Fourth Amendment concerns and warned plate data can be bought and sold.

records.Name: Stacy L. Ball
records.What: Will discontinue Flock, will not renew, and will not replace the cameras with Axon.

records.Name: Josh Verscheure
records.What: Ending the Flock partnership on August 31, citing public trust. Distinct from Henry County, Virginia and Missouri.

records.Name: Aaron N. Brown
records.What: Will not renew the Flock LPR agreement when the grant-funded term expires March 11, 2027.

records.Name: Wayne Davis
records.What: Suspended access and started dismantling 14 cameras. Exploring early termination of a contract through August 2028.

records.Name: Dave Daniel
records.What: Canceled a 10-camera Flock contract and deactivated the cameras the same day, citing Fourth Amendment concerns.

records.Name: Ross Teeple
records.What: Will not renew the operational contract when it expires September 29, citing Fourth Amendment concerns.
